recentItems.title: Trump rejects tech industry’s calls for AI slowdown
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has brushed aside concerns raised by AI leaders – including Elon Musk, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman – about the pace of its development, branding them "very negative forces".

Trump says the US must maintain its dominance over China in artificial intelligence, despite dire warnings from insiders it could lead to the extinction of the human race.

As the AI alarm bells continue to grow louder, Australia's government says it’s taking these calls from the tech industry for a slowdown seriously.

recentItems.title: Trailblazing judge Mary Gaudron dies aged 83
recentItems.description:
Pioneering Australian judge Mary Gaudron has been honoured for her contributions to Australia's legal landscape after her death at age 83.

Gaudron became the first woman appointed to the High Court of Australia, breaking ground in the male-dominated profession.

recentItems.title: New bill seeks consistent definition of affordable housing
recentItems.description:
New federal legislation is seeking to make the definition of affordable housing consistent across the country.

Independent MP Nicolette Boele has introduced a bill to make sure renters, including frontline workers, can rely on the definition of affordable.

The move has been welcomed by housing groups and the property industry.

recentItems.title: Whyalla steelworks to cut more than 500 jobs
recentItems.description:
Hundreds of employees at South Australia's Whyalla steelworks are set to lose their jobs after the operation's ageing blast furnace repeatedly failed to fire.

Located about 380 kilometres north of Adelaide, the decision to abandon further revival efforts will effectively shut down most of the manufacturing at one of Australia's two remaining steel facilities.

recentItems.title: Indonesian ramps up search for 129 people missing after ferry capsizes
recentItems.description:
Six people have now been confirmed dead, with another 129 still missing, after a passenger ferry capsized in the Java Sea.

Indonesian authorities say they are ramping up the search, deploying more than 600 rescue personnel – but rough conditions are hampering their efforts.

SBS International Correspondent Claudia Farhart has more from Jakarta.

For more news: https://bit.ly/3qBhrgi

recentItems.title: One Nation reveals plans to cut migration by 750,000
recentItems.description:
Pauline Hanson has drawn widespread political condemnation over her comments about the contribution of First Nations Australians. 

The controversy has become a diversion for One Nation which has revealed its policy to dramatically cut migration by 750,000.

recentItems.title: Russian drone strikes Ukraine train | Fighting intensifes in Yemen | Oil price spike fears
recentItems.description:
Russia is accused of targeting foreign diplomats in a drone strike near Poland's border with Ukraine. 

The drone hit a passenger train in an attack likely targeting the former prime ministers of the UK and Sweden according to Ukraine's railway operator.

Russia said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine. 

Poland and Ukraine have denounced the attack.

recentItems.title: Swedish election too close to call as far-right loses ground
recentItems.description:
Sweden's general election remains too close to call, with the final result not expected until later this week. 

Projected results have given the left-wing political bloc, led by the Social Democrats, a slim majority over the rival four-party coalition, put together by current conservative prime minister Ulf Kristersson.

The results also show support for the far-right anti-immigration Sweden Democrats has dropped for the first time.

For more on this story: https://bit.ly/3Tp9lGp

recentItems.title: Difficult snow season leaves businesses counting cost
recentItems.description:
Snow tourism has taken a hit with nearly all Australian ski resorts shutting a month earlier than usual.

Parts of south-eastern Australia have experienced the hottest winter on record, as the El Niño weather pattern combines with a warming climate.

In the Victorian High Country town of Mansfield and nearby Mount Buller, businesses that rely on winter tourism have been forced to adapt after a disappointing snow season.

recentItems.title: Borneo’s last orangutans under threat from severe wildfires
recentItems.description:
The island of Borneo is home to more than 80 per cent of the world's remaining orangutans.

But decades of land clearing for agriculture, logging and mining have destroyed vast swathes of their forests and left them critically endangered.

Now severe wildfires fuelled by a severe and strengthening El Niño are putting even more of their habitat in danger of destruction.

SBS International Correspondent Claudia Farhart visited the Sebangau National Park in Central Kalimantan – where a team of researchers dedicate their days and nights to protecting the great apes.

recentItems.title: Maximum restraint called for in Middle East at BRICs summit
recentItems.description:
World leaders gathered in New Delhi for the two-day BRICS summit have issued a joint statement, calling for maximum restraint in the Middle East and a pause on unilateral acts of aggression. 

The joint statement also calls for an end to Israeli violence in Gaza, support for the UN agency that delivers aid to Palestinian refugees, and full United Nations membership for Palestine, while notably omitting reference to the war in Ukraine.
